title: Willow
about: A farmer from a village of little people is chosen to carry a special baby to safety.
cue: Serve the snacks when Willow first meets Madmartigan in the crow's cage at the crossroads.

Nelwyn Village FairWillowMagic acorns. Bigger appetite.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersWillow's magic acorn bitesBocconcini in hazelnut, like Willow's acorn threatHow to make it100g hazelnuts1 tbsp chopped chives250g bocconcini2 tbsp honeyToast the hazelnuts at 180°C, rub off the skins and chop finely. Mix with the chives.Pat the bocconcini dry and roll each ball in the hazelnut mix so it looks like a little acorn.Arrange on a plate and drizzle with a little honey.Nelwyn harvest breadWarm homemade rolls served with parsley and chive butterHow to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast20g butter, soft, for the dough300ml warm water1 tsp salt100g butter, soft, for serving1 tbsp chopped parsley1 tbsp chopped chives200g brieMix the flour, yeast, salt, the butter for the dough and warm water to a dough and knead until smooth.Prove the dough for an hour until doubled.Shape into rolls and bake at 200°C until golden.Mash the butter for serving with the parsley and chives. Serve the warm rolls with it and a wedge of brie.Roast chestnuts with sea saltMadmartigan's view from the crow cage.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsTavern brawl beef and root veg stewBeef chuck, carrots and parsnips simmered 3 hours in tomato beef stockHow to make it1kg beef chuck, diced1 brown onion, sliced3 carrots, cut into chunks2 parsnips, cut into chunks1 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp tomato paste1 L beef stock1 tsp thyme leaves1 bay leaf1 loaf crusty bread50g butter2 tbsp oilBrown the beef in the oil in batches.Add the onion, carrots and parsnips and cook for 5 minutes.Stir in the flour and tomato paste, then the stock, thyme and bay leaf.Cover and simmer for 3 hours until the beef is tender and the sauce is rich.Serve in bowls with crusty bread and butter.Nockmaar fennel crackling porkBavmorda: "You're all pigs!"How to make itAs written, serves 4Pork shoulder scored and rubbed with salt and fennel seed, roasted slow until tender, the crackling blasted until it shatters, with roast apples and potatoes.Score the skin of a 2kg pork shoulder, rub with salt and 2 tsp crushed fennel seeds and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Roast at 160°C for 4 hours.Add 1kg potatoes and 4 halved apples tossed in oil for the last hour.Turn up to 240°C for 25 minutes until the crackling blisters.Rest 15 minutes and carve.SweetsNockmaar castle blackberry tartBlackberries pressed into almond cream in a sweet pastry shellHow to make it1 sheet sweet shortcrust pastry100g butter, soft100g caster sugar2 eggs100g almond meal300g frozen blackberries2 tbsp icing sugar300ml thick creamLine a 23cm tart tin with the pastry and chill for 20 minutes.Beat the butter and sugar, then the eggs and almond meal. Spread in the case and press in the blackberries.Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until golden and set.Cool, dust with icing sugar and serve with thick cream.Brownies' berry and cream tartletsFranjean and Rool, the troublesome browniesHow to make itAs written, serves 4Tiny crisp pastry cases filled with vanilla whipped cream and piled with mixed berries tossed in sugar and lemon zest, finished with icing sugar.Cut 2 sheets of sweet shortcrust into 24 rounds and press into a mini muffin tray.Prick and bake at 190°C for 12 minutes until golden, then cool.Toss 300g mixed berries with 1 tbsp caster sugar and the zest of a lemon.Whip 200ml cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and vanilla.Spoon cream into the cases, pile on the berries and dust with icing sugar.DrinksNelwyn warm spiced apple punchWarm apple juice with cinnamon, cloves, orange peel and honeyHow to make it1.5 L cloudy apple juice2 cinnamon sticks6 whole cloves1 orange, peeled into strips1 tbsp honey1 apple, thinly slicedPour the apple juice into a pot with the cinnamon, cloves, orange peel and honey.Warm gently for 15 minutes without boiling so the spices come through. Strain out the cloves.Ladle into mugs and float a thin apple slice in each.Elderberry cordialFranjean and Rool want theirs in thimbles.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
